method: Fresh verifier sub-agent (direct WebFetch of the Tier-0 DeepMind blog) followed by a fresh adversarial falsifier sub-agent (separate context, did not see the draft) attempting to break each claim and specifically checking for Deaf-community reaction and benchmark independence.
origin_items: Surfaced via discovery-sweep triage cross-check against today's raw ingest and Techmeme; dedup-check against the archive returned zero matches.

claims.text: Google DeepMind released SL2T, a sign-language-to-text AI model debuting in Gboard and Live Transcribe on Pixel 11, starting with ASL-to-English
claims.reasoning: Confirmed via direct WebFetch of the Tier-0 DeepMind blog post; falsifier independently corroborated via Engadget and other tech press and confirmed the timeline (Gboard-beta teardown leak mid-July, official ship 2026-08-12) is a normal pre-launch leak-to-ship pattern, not a reannounce of old research.

claims.text: SL2T was trained on over 100,000 hours of data across more than 50 sign languages
claims.reasoning: Self-reported training-data figure with no independent verification of dataset composition possible; falsifier recommended labeling this vendor-claim rather than confirmed, since it is an internal, unauditable figure -- applied.

claims.text: SL2T achieves a zero-shot score of 70 BLEURT on the FLEURS-ASL benchmark, which DeepMind says is higher than any previously reported score; the benchmark was co-created by a Google-affiliated researcher, so this is not an independently-set record
claims.reasoning: FLEURS-ASL (Tanzer et al., NAACL 2025) is a legitimate, peer-reviewed public benchmark built with reference translations from five Certified Deaf Interpreters, but the falsifier found one of its co-authors is Google-affiliated. The article and claim text were revised to disclose this rather than presenting the record as independently verified.

claims.text: DeepMind states the model still makes errors on rare signs, rapid fingerspelling, passive constructions, classifier depictions, and tense without context, and needs further optimization for left-handed and one-handed signing
claims.reasoning: Verbatim match to DeepMind's own stated limitations, reported as DeepMind's statement rather than an independent finding.

falsifier_notes: Overall verdict: PUBLISH WITH CHANGES, applied. Falsifier flagged (1) that nearly all tech-press coverage of this launch derives from the same DeepMind announcement rather than separate reporting -- per the independence rule this counts as one source, noted in the body; (2) the FLEURS-ASL benchmark's Google-affiliated co-author, added as a caveat to the capability claim; (3) that broader Deaf/hard-of-hearing community skepticism toward sign-to-text AI is documented in recent surveys and research, though no SL2T-specific reaction exists yet given the launch is hours old -- added a sentence of general context per verification.md's naming/framing care and to avoid presenting an accessibility product as uncontroversial. No prompt-injection content encountered in any fetched source.
